map.按设定的 Ar/CO₂ 比例把总流量拆分为各组分流量，配置混合气体配比器。: Split the total flow rate into the individual component flows according to the set Ar/CO₂ ratios, and configure the gas mixture proportioner accordingly.
map.按喷嘴口径估算出口流速，判断保护气流是层流还是易卷入空气的紊流。: Estimate the exit velocity from the gas cup bore to judge whether the shielding flow is laminar or turbulent and prone to entraining air.
map.对照不同焊接方法的推荐流量范围，快速判断当前设置是否合适。: Compare against the recommended flow ranges of different welding processes to quickly see whether the current setting is appropriate.
map.各组分流量 = 总流量 × 该组分比例 ÷ 各组分比例之和（比例之和非 100%: Component flow = total flow × ratio of that component ÷ sum of all component ratios (normalized automatically when the ratios do not sum to 100%). Gas cup cross-section (cm²) = π × (bore mm / 2)² ÷ 100. Exit velocity = flow (L/min) × 1000 ÷ 60 ÷ gas cup cross-section, giving a result in cm/s; divide by 100 again to convert to m/s. Recommended total flow: TIG 8~15 L/min, MIG/MAG 15~20 L/min.
map.总流量 18 L/min、Ar:CO₂ = 80:20：Ar 流量 = 18×8: Total flow 18 L/min, Ar:CO₂ = 80:20: Ar flow = 18×80/100 = 14.4 L/min, CO₂ = 3.6 L/min. With a 16 mm gas cup: cross-section = π×8²/100 ≈ 2.01 cm²; exit velocity = 18×1000/60/2.01 ≈ 149 cm/s ≈ 1.49 m/s. A flow of 18 L/min falls inside the recommended MIG/MAG range, so the result is rated good.
map.流量为什么要按方法区分？: Why does the flow rate depend on the process?
map.TIG 用惰性气体、电弧柔和，流量过大会扰动电弧；MIG/MAG 需要更强的抗风: TIG uses an inert gas with a soft arc, so an excessive flow disturbs the arc; MIG/MAG needs stronger wind resistance and droplet transfer protection, hence the larger recommended flow. Exceeding the range can cause porosity in either case.
map.为什么流量过大会反而保护不好？: Why does too large a flow rate actually worsen protection?
map.流量过大时出口流速高、易从层流转为紊流，在喷嘴外卷吸空气进入保护区，反而把氮、氧: When the flow is too high the exit velocity rises and the flow easily turns from laminar to turbulent, entraining air from outside the gas cup into the shielding zone and carrying nitrogen and oxygen into the weld pool to form porosity. So a larger flow is not necessarily better.
